items.note: S2 speaks of 'fixed linear exchange networks' on W roles and S3 of arbitrary auxiliary values, but no step gives the eight-row schedule, the update y_S <- y_S + x_S, the three-stage signed exchange (X,Y)->(-Y,X) or the restoration of scratch wires.

S2.1 has the frames D_v, pointwise gates commuting with them and an endpoint operator on each role. It omits the edge operator D_vD_u^{-1}, the implemented operator D_out S D_in^{-1} and the route formula eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}.

S2.2 says gates are labelled by nested subspaces of an m-dimensional space built from triples. It gives no orthogonality of neighbouring triples, no L=Ich, no budget Wm-2N+2L and no bound L<N/2, so the budget that yields the saving is not stated. Conservative choice between mentioned and stated.

S3's method realises the bit network on tape with edge operators factored into shears. Neither the endpoint condition M_sink - M_source = I_m, nor the resulting shear H <- H+D, nor s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b appears.
S4.2 alludes to phase frames expressing a C tensor product. It gives no definition of C_U, no factorisation of edge changes into one kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector, and no count s_c.

The plan states s<Wm and s/W<m^tau with tau<1. It never gives tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, the deficits eta_b, eta_c or the log m<20 argument, and it does not tie s<Wm to L<N/2. S2.3 presents s/W<m^tau as following from the recursion's shape.
The only trace is 'lower triangular shears performed in linear time' / 'plus linear work'. The elementary stream operations and controlled shifts y <- y + a(controls) mod q^b are not stated.

S3.1 states the shear (H,D)->(H+AD,D) of rank a costs a interchanges of b-digit fields plus linear work, via reversed-order lower triangular (Bruhat) factors. It omits the explicit A=E_1 Pi E_2 and the H-D pairing of interchanges. It then says 'on u-digit fields', which is inconsistent with b.

S2/S2.3 give the recursion: s calls on volume V/W per node, so cost V times a sub-linear power of the parameter. Missing are the role-stream split, the shear H <- H+D, the three-shear swap D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D, the O(1) per-node overhead with its fixed-tape schedule, and the conditions (row field divisible by W^k).
S3.2 quotes the lemma's permutation (p,h,g,d,z)->(p,d,g,h,z) in O(Vu^tau) for arbitrary u. The reduction to power widths is only named in S3's method ('remove width and row restrictions').

S4.2 paraphrases the paper's overview: phase frames express a C tensor product through smaller groups of selected bits separated by binary changes of basis. It omits the conjugation by P_M that moves kernels to coordinate slots, the s_c child calls, the inverse-kernel identity and H_0^{otimes D} = b^D S C^{otimes D} S. It also calls the frames 'diagonal', though they are only diagonalised by H^{otimes m}.
S4.2 only says binary changes of basis are 'done by moving whole chunks'. The eight cyclic shifts, the bad set and its sorting repair, and the cost are absent.

S4's motivation invokes 'the same rank-saving recursion over selected bits'. The rows from the first q_0 chunks, the recurrence F(e) <= (s/W)F(e/m) + O((eK)^tau+1), the cutoff at d^beta and the resulting d^{lambda'} are not given.

The statement (H_0 on one bit of up to d chunks in O(Vd^{lambda'}), exact dyadic evaluation, one truncation) is right but omits K=floor(d^c), the error bound below sqrt2 2^{-p} and the guard width. The sub-steps follow the paper's outline, but the recursive volume reduction by splitting rows among roles and the guard-bit bound are missing.

Correctly gives omega_t=y^{2r/t}, radix-two butterflies, retained frequency order and a layout placing selected bits at a common chunk offset. It omits F_t^+F_t^- = t^{-1}I, the exact counterparts LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}, the error and the cost O(Tp[dK+pK^{tau-1}+l d^{lambda'}]).

The route (signed Kronecker substitution, established multiplier, unpacking to exact fg and Q_p(fg/r), O(rp log(rp))) matches. Missing are the four real/imaginary numerator products, the radix B_0=2^{4p}, the centred-residue recovery and the reduction mod y^r+1; 'packed into one integer' is loose.

The route (two forward transforms in retained order, pointwise ring products, opposite transform) is the paper's. The normalisation (f*g)/(rM), the error sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p}, the cost and the exact scale by M are not given. S5.4 refers only to 'the stated error'.

States that coprime-length transforms reduce to power-of-two tensor transforms by Gaussian resampling, with permutations retained and maps applied linewise using chunk interchange. It gives neither the identity P_sF_s = 2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA, its hypotheses, nor the costs.

S7.3 correctly says the chirp identity turns the middle factor into a cyclic convolution between phase multiplications without applying the target permutation. Neither identity is written. S7.1 has both permutations cancelling, whereas the paper absorbs Q into the chirp and only R cancels.
S8.1 names a fixed rational choice and gives only kappa=2^{-182}. The other values, the sizes (b, p=6b, d, K, T, r) and the choice of the prime source lengths s_i are absent.

S8.2 states that a CRT address map puts the coefficients on pairwise coprime prime cyclic axes and preserves convolution. It lacks Phi: x -> prod x_i^{mu_i}, its triangular mixed-radix form and the cost.

S8.3 states x_d -> zeta y turns the last cyclic coordinate into R_r, with the negative wrap reproducing the cyclic wrap. It does not specify zeta=e^{pi i/r} or give M_C = D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g).

S8's method lists the stages (radix digits, prime axes, twist, run, precision). The source transform as composition 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A = RF_s, its conjugate, and the six-step algorithm with the scalings by S and 2^{2b+4}S are not stated.

S8.5 has the 2^{-p} grid and a final coefficient error below 1/2 permitting exact rounding and carries. It gives no quantities (p=6b, E_s, E_w, the 448b 2^{-3b/4} bound, gamma<=b/4) and says errors 'add', ignoring the amplification by 2^gamma, S and T^2.
R and S8.6 state the final bound O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}), kappa=2^{-182}, from cost terms divided by V=Theta(n). The table's terms, the margins g_1..g_7 and min g_i = 2^{-181} = 2 kappa are not given.
R only lists 'conjecture' among its prerequisites and motivates against Theta(n log n) scanning. The lower-bound formulation and its negation via liminf are absent.

errors.says: Labelling gates by subspaces makes adjacent edge operators nested.
errors.paper: The labels at the two ends of each edge are nested; the edge's change of frame is cheap in proportion to the orthogonal residual dimension. Edge operators are not nested.

errors.says: A call at parameter mf uses s calls at parameter f on volume V/W, so s/W<m^tau with tau<1.
errors.paper: s/W<m^tau follows from the explicit rank deficits eta_b, eta_c > 20*2^{-50} and log m<20, not from the recursion's shape.

errors.says: The shear uses a interchanges of b-digit fields ... on u-digit fields.
errors.paper: Every field ranges over [q^b] and the interchanges are of b-digit fields; u is the bit width in the arbitrary-width lemma.

errors.says: Diagonal phase frames express a tensor product of C.
errors.paper: The frames are C_U = H^{otimes m} diag(i^{q_U}) H^{otimes m}, diagonalised by H^{otimes m} but not themselves diagonal.

errors.says: Signed coefficients are packed into one integer so that the polynomial product becomes an integer product.
errors.paper: Real and imaginary numerator polynomials are evaluated separately at B_0=2^{4p} and four integer products are made.

errors.says: The source and target coordinate permutations are kept inside the formula so they cancel across the forward transforms, product and inverse.
errors.paper: The target permutation Q is absorbed into the chirp convolution; only the source permutation R cancels in the convolution identity.
Errors pass through contractions but are amplified by the scalings 2^gamma, S and 2^{2b+4}S, giving E_w < 28 2^gamma T^2 L and the final bound 448b 2^{-3b/4}.

chain: The tree follows the paper's architecture: power-saving network, then chunk interchange and the simultaneous butterfly layer, then synthetic transforms and convolution, Gaussian resampling with chirp, and finally parameters, precision and cost. Each link is mostly a quoted assertion. The scalar bank exchange, the label budget L<N/2 and the two rational and phase interfaces are only alluded to, so the source of s<Wm is unexplained. The recurrences (eq:swap-recurrence and the layer's F(e)) and the final error chain and cost margins appear only as conclusions without their quantities.
